answer: Bonded identity oracles make fake agents expensive to certify: independent oracle nodes stake real bonds and attest that each identity is unique, like an opal graded once and only once. Their verdicts rise like a plume through the network, and any oracle caught certifying a nebula of sock-puppets loses its bond. A sybil farm must therefore bribe or corrupt many bonded oracles at once, and each lie it buys risks the very stake that made the oracle trusted.
